reason: Phase 11d/11e/11f: precision and severity, with the denominator deliberately untouched (callSites identical on all five repos: 1326/352/95/3774/2954). 11d - no-deep-css-chain measures depth per selector from the tokenizer, so a comma list is no longer a chain: 5 findings removed across the checkouts, 4 in the analyzed set (all comma lists, e.g. 'strong em, em strong'), 0 added. It now has NO corpus evidence at all (fires on 0 of 5 repos), as does no-nth-child - both are covered only by unit tests, which is worth knowing when reading this record. 11e - .nth() moves out of no-nth-child into avoid-positional-access at warn: a 1:1 swap (cal.com 113, documenso 126, mattermost 29, immich 6, Ghost 2), no count change. no-nth-child also widened from a ':nth-child(' substring to the parsed pseudo, which additionally covers :nth-last-child (corpus-neutral). 11f - locator('..') moves out of no-xpath into avoid-parent-traversal at info: 9 of the 11 xpath findings were the '..' idiom, so the error-level rule was mostly reporting the quiet case. Scores rise (cal.com 69->74, immich 89->91, Ghost 98->99, documenso 89->91, mattermost 66->67), dominated by the two severity reductions: cal.com is 113 findings x 3 weight points plus one xpath finding x 4.5 = 343.5 / (1326 x 5) = 5.18%. Not from the denominator: extracting .first()/.last() would add ~10% more call sites and move every score a further 3-8 points, so it is deferred to Phase 12 which owns the denominator. Correction: an earlier version of this reason said '6 of 8' xpath findings and 'exactly 5.1%'. Both were wrong. The 6-of-8 came from a probe script that scanned only single-quoted .locator() calls in spec files rather than the analyzer's own extraction - the third time in this phase that measuring with a different code path than the shipped rule produced a wrong published number.
